title: Personal Training Packages: valuing the unused sessions at refund by proration basis
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Personal Training Packages product line and states how the dollar value of a package's unused sessions is computed at refund, according to the tier's own proration basis.

## Rule
On a proration basis of sessions used, the unused-session value is the unused-session count multiplied by the package's own per-session value, where the per-session value is the tier's own listed purchase amount divided by the tier's own granted session count. On a proration basis of percentage elapsed, the unused-session value is instead the tier's own listed purchase amount multiplied by the fraction of the tier's own expiration window that has not yet elapsed since the package's purchase date. Only one of these two bases is ever used for a given package, according to that tier's own proration basis; the two are never combined or averaged.

## Points of judgement
- Sessions-used basis: the per-session value is derived by dividing the tier's own listed purchase amount by the tier's own granted session count, and the unused-session value is that per-session value multiplied by however many sessions remain unused on the package.
- Percentage-elapsed basis: the elapsed fraction is the number of full calendar days since the purchase date divided by the tier's own expiration window in days; the remaining, not-yet-elapsed fraction is what is multiplied against the tier's own listed purchase amount, and the remaining fraction is never allowed below zero.
For example, on a percentage-elapsed tier, a package exactly halfway through its expiration window (with half the window's days already elapsed) has a remaining fraction of one half, so its unused-session value is one half of the tier's own listed purchase amount; a package at the very end of its window, with the full window already elapsed, has a remaining fraction of zero and an unused-session value of zero, even though the package may still nominally hold unused sessions.
